short: Britain and France secretly agreed to partition the crumbling Ottoman Empire into spheres of influence.
full:
On 16 May 1916, the governments of the United Kingdom and France, with the assent of the Russian Empire and Italy, finalized a secret treaty defining their mutually agreed spheres of influence and control in Southwestern Asia. Negotiated by diplomats Mark Sykes and François Georges-Picot, the agreement anticipated the defeat of the Ottoman Empire.

The treaty effectively divided the Arab provinces of the Ottoman Empire outside the Arabian Peninsula into areas of direct British and French control or indirect influence. The agreement contradicted British promises made to Arab leaders regarding a unified Arab state in exchange for rebelling against the Ottomans, planting the seeds for a century of geopolitical instability in the Middle East.
